text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove repeated sections. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after the changes. By refactoring regularly, developers can reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design make future changes harder. In short, refactoring keeps code healthy and helps teams work faster over time.
